extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings), counsel, and OED/USPTO staff
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for an affidavit of resignation and approval of exclusion on consent under 37 C.F.R. § 11.27, including required acknowledgments by the respondent, publication duties, compliance obligations, and consequences for reinstatement. Targets practitioners subject to USPTO discipline and the Office of Enrollment and Discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit of Resignation must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Respondent's Affidavit of Resignation must comply with the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a); the Director will review and approve the affidavit submitted by the OED Director for the purpose of excluding a practitioner on consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the affidavit complies with § 11.27(a), the Director may approve it and order exclusion on consent. The Final Order states: 'Respondent's Affidavit of Resignation complies with the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a). Hence, it is ORDERED that... Respondent's Affidavit of Resignation shall be, and hereby is, approved.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary consent / no coercion
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must acknowledge that 'Her consent is freely and voluntarily rendered, and she is not being subjected to coercion or duress.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit should contain an express statement that consent to exclusion is given freely and voluntarily; lack of such a statement may undermine validity of exclusion-on-consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of pending disciplinary investigation and basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must acknowledge awareness that 'there is a disciplinary investigation currently pending against her and that the investigation is based upon allegations of misconduct predicated upon certain acts' (the affidavit here cites the guilty plea/conviction and the underlying factual conduct).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit should describe the pending investigation or the allegations forming its basis so the respondent is aware of what is being resolved by the resignation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of implicated Disciplinary Rules (specific rule citations)
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit/record may identify specific Disciplinary Rules the OED believes were violated — here 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(5) (proscribing engaging in conduct that is prejudicial to the administration of justice) and 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(a) via 10.23(c)(1) (proscribing conviction of a criminal offense involving breach of trust).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When OED asserts particular rule violations, the affidavit or accompanying documents should reference the specific regulatory provisions implicated so the nature of the alleged misconduct is clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-admission with reinstatement presumption (37 C.F.R. § 11.60 consequence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent may not admit the violations but must acknowledge that 'if and when she applies for reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60, the OED Director will conclusively presume, for the limited purpose of determining the application for reinstatement, that (i) the allegations implicated in the pending investigation ... are true and (ii) she could not have successfully defended herself against such allegations.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavits of resignation often include this concession to make clear the evidentiary presumption that will apply on any future reinstatement application under § 11.60.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge and understanding of governing regulations and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must acknowledge having 'fully read and understands 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.27, 11.58, 11.59, and 11.60, and is fully aware of the legal and factual consequences of requesting and consenting to exclusion from practice before the USPTO.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit should state that the respondent understands the cited regulatory provisions and the legal effects of consenting to exclusion (including publication, effect on privileges, and reinstatement process).

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's authority to approve and exclude (statutory/regulatory basis)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director's authority to approve an affidavit of resignation and to exclude a practitioner on consent is grounded in 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.27.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any approval/exclusion order should cite the statutory and regulatory authority for the action; practitioners and OED should rely on these provisions when processing or challenging exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order effect: exclusion from practice effective upon signing
rubrics_metrics.description: Once approved, 'Respondent shall be, and hereby is, excluded on consent from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the Office beginning on the date this Final Order is signed.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final Orders must state the effective date of exclusion; exclusion-on-consent terminates the practitioner's ability to practice before the USPTO as of that date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication obligations (OED Reading Room and Official Gazette)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room (http://des.uspto.gov/Foia/OEDReadingRoom.jsp) and publish a notice in the Official Gazette describing the exclusion on consent and relevant facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary decisions and notices of exclusion are made public per the cited regs; the Final Order sets out sample Official Gazette language and requires posting in the OED Reading Room.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with §§ 11.58, 11.59, and 11.60 (respondent and OED duties)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order requires that 'Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58; The OED Director shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59; Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This sets out mutual duties: § 11.58 concerns effect of resolution on pending matters, § 11.59 concerns publication and notice, and § 11.60 governs reinstatement procedure and standards; both respondent and OED must follow these provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent 'shall bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this agreement.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order can specify how costs are allocated; in this case each side bears its own costs — practitioners and counsel should note potential cost consequences when negotiating an affidavit of resignation.
